source.title: Good linear classifiers are abundant in the interpolating regime
source.authors: Ryan Theisen; J. Klusowski; Michael W. Mahoney

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites double-descent work as context but does not test or rely on the double-descent claim. Its own results concern distributions of test errors among interpolating classifiers, not a double-descent curve.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-error concentration as dimension or feature count grows, and a theoretical test-error result as sample count grows. These are related to the claim's subject but do not test a fall-rise-fall curve, its interpolation-threshold peak, epoch-wise behavior, or an increase in error from adding data near that threshold. Double-descent results mentioned in the introduction are cited from other work and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper cites double-descent results only as context in the introduction. Its own results are distributions of test errors among interpolating linear and random-feature classifiers at fixed aspect ratios, plus an asymptotic critical-value theorem. None traces test error across the interpolation threshold over size, epochs or samples, so no version is tested. All experiments stay in the interpolating regime (n < d or n/N = α < 1).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. More precisely: almost all interpolating classifiers' test errors concentrate around a small critical value ε*, far below the worst-case interpolator's error. The authors argue that uniform-convergence analysis is too coarse and that statistical-mechanics, typical-case analysis is a promising alternative.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses conditional distributions over interpolating classifiers and analyzes test-error concentration; it does not apply the original double-descent measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported critical error depends on aspect ratio and task difficulty; in the Gaussian model it also depends on SNR, and in the theoretical model it depends on ρ and n.

fits_no_version.finding: Among interpolating linear and random ReLU feature classifiers, test errors concentrate around a critical value ε*(α) as dimension or feature count grows. ε* depends on task difficulty, SNR and aspect ratio.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test-error distributions over the version space concentrate at a typical value far below the worst-case interpolator's error.

fits_no_version.finding: Under equicorrelated data, ε* = (1−ρ)/(nρ) as nρ → ∞.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the equicorrelated model, the typical interpolating classifier's error decays as O(1/n).

record.problems: The paper studies linear and random-feature classifiers rather than general neural networks. Empirical distributions use M = 10,000 LIN-ESS samples with 1,000 warm-up samples and every 10th sample retained; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The theoretical result uses a simplified equicorrelation assumption. The paper does not measure double-descent curves.
record.rows_left_out: No additional findings were omitted for the claim; cited results from other work were excluded.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep across the interpolation threshold, and no deep networks.
No training-time axis; classifiers are sampled, not trained.
No sample sweep near the interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep past the interpolation point.
No effective-complexity measure or peak location is studied.
No label-noise or regularization manipulation, and no multiple peaks.

missing.what: Worst-case interpolating classifiers built from appended 'bad' points reach test error near 1, against typical errors near 5% (MNIST, n=350). This is not a double-descent result, but it is a main finding absent from the rows.

record.verdict_notes: Double descent appears only in the introduction's literature citations, including Belkin et al. (an original source). Relation cites_only / T6 is confirmed.

versions.untested_parts: No isolated model-size sweep measuring a fall-rise-fall test-error curve or a peak near the interpolation threshold.
No test of whether adding training samples raises error near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across the interpolation point that measures a second descent.
No test of whether a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across axes.
No test of label-noise or regularization effects on a double-descent peak, or of triple or multiple descent.
No re-counting of complexity to assess whether a second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: Gaussian mixture distribution
rows.operation_detail: Vary dimension while keeping the aspect ratio α = n/d fixed in each setting.
rows.measure: Distribution of test errors among interpolating linear classifiers; concentration around critical value ε*
rows.value: As d grows, distributions appear to approach 1(ε ≥ ε*); ε* depends on α and SNR.
rows.note: The text describes concentration, not a double-descent curve; dimension and sample count vary together at fixed aspect ratio.
rows.check: Dimension and n vary together at fixed α inside the interpolating regime. The row measures concentration of the error distribution, not a capacity curve.

rows.subject: random ReLU feature classifiers on MNIST (0 vs 1)
rows.size_stated: N varies; exact values not stated in the text
rows.operation_detail: Vary the number of random ReLU features with α = n/N settings.
rows.measure: Distribution of test errors among interpolating classifiers
rows.value: As N grows, test errors begin to concentrate around ε*(α).
rows.note: The reported result is concentration at fixed aspect-ratio settings, not the claimed model-size fall-rise-fall shape.
rows.check: N grows at fixed α = n/N. No sweep crosses the interpolation threshold.

rows.subject: random ReLU feature classifiers on FASHION-MNIST (shirt vs pants)
rows.size_stated: N varies; exact values not stated in the text
rows.operation_detail: Vary the number of random ReLU features with α = n/N settings.
rows.measure: Distribution of test errors among interpolating classifiers
rows.value: As N grows, test errors begin to concentrate around ε*(α); the critical value is larger for this task than for MNIST.
rows.note: The reported result is concentration at fixed aspect-ratio settings, not the claimed model-size fall-rise-fall shape.

rows.subject: equicorrelated Gaussian classification setting
rows.operation_detail: Analyze the asymptotic critical test-error value as the number of training samples n grows.
rows.measure: Critical value ε* of the test-error distribution
rows.note: This is an asymptotic result in a simplified correlation model, not a test of increasing data near an interpolation threshold.
rows.check: Asymptotic result under equicorrelation. ε* falls monotonically in n, but there is no interpolation threshold in this model to test V3.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
